description: Use this when you want something given to you. Just place a noun before 주세요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 물 주세요. (Water, please.) or 메뉴 주세요. (Menu, please.).
Point at anything and ask what it is. Just place a noun before 뭐예요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 이거 뭐예요? (What is this?) or 저거 뭐예요? (What is that?).
Ask if something exists or is available. Just place a noun before 있어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 자리 있어요? (Is there a seat?) or 와이파이 있어요? (Is there Wi-Fi?).

Ask how to get to a specific place. Just place a noun before 어떻게 가요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 명동에 어떻게 가요? (How do I get to Myeongdong?) or 지하철역에 어떻게 가요? (How do I get to the subway station?).

examples.en: How do I get to Myeongdong?
How do I get to the subway station?
How do I get to the airport?

description: Say where you want to go. Just place a noun before 가고 싶어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 제주도에 가고 싶어요. (I want to go to Jeju Island.) or 바다에 가고 싶어요. (I want to go to the sea.).

examples.en: I want to go to Jeju Island.
I want to go to the sea.
I want to go to Seoul.

description: Decide on one option when ordering or choosing. Just place a noun before 로 할게요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 이걸로 할게요. (I'll go with this one.) or 아메리카노로 할게요. (I'll have the Americano.).

Ask if someone has ever experienced something before. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 한국 음식 먹어 본 적 있어요? (Have you ever tried Korean food?) or 서울에 가 본 적 있어요? (Have you ever been to Seoul?).

examples.en: Have you ever tried Korean food?
examples.ko: 한국 음식 먹어 본 적 있어요?

examples.en: Have you ever been to Seoul?

description: Ask someone to give you a recommendation. Just place a noun before 추천해 주세요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 메뉴 추천해 주세요. (Please recommend something from the menu.) or 숙소 추천해 주세요. (Please recommend a place to stay.).

examples.en: Please recommend something from the menu.
Please recommend a place to stay.

description: Politely request someone to do something for you. Say what you need, then add 주실 수 있어요 at the end. Common uses: 사진 찍어 주실 수 있어요? (Could you take a photo for me?) or 도와주실 수 있어요? (Could you help me?).

examples.en: Could you take a photo for me?

description: Say what you like or enjoy. Say what you need, then add 좋아해요 at the end. Common uses: 한국 음식 좋아해요. (I like Korean food.) or 케이팝 좋아해요. (I like K-pop.).

Express that something is surprisingly fascinating or unique. Say what you need, then add 신기해요 at the end. Common uses: 이 음식 신기해요. (This food is fascinating.) or 한국 문화가 신기해요. (Korean culture is really fascinating.).

Politely ask for a lower price on something. Just place a noun before 깎아 주세요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 좀 깎아 주세요. (Please give me a discount.) or 만 원만 깎아 주세요. (Please discount 10,000 won.).

examples.en: Please lower the price a little.

description: Ask if someone has ever tried using something. Say what you need, then add 써봤어요 at the end. Common uses: 이 앱 써봤어요? (Have you tried this app?) or 이 크림 써봤어요? (Have you tried this cream?).
Ask which option someone prefers. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 어떤 색이 좋아요? (Which color do you like?) or 어떤 맛이 좋아요? (Which flavor do you like?).

examples.en: Which one do you like among these?

description: Say something is more or less than you expected. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 생각보다 맛있어요. (It's tastier than I expected.) or 생각보다 멀어요. (It's farther than I thought.).

Say you feel nervous or excited about something important. Just place a noun before 떨려요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 너무 떨려요. (I'm so nervous.) or 첫날이라 떨려요. (I'm nervous because it's the first day.).

examples.en: I'm nervous because it's the first day.
I'm nervous because I have a presentation.

description: Say which country or city you come from. Just place a noun before 에서 왔어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 미국에서 왔어요. (I'm from the United States.) or 영국에서 왔어요. (I'm from the United Kingdom.).

Use when meeting someone to ask for their cooperation. Say what you need, then add 잘 부탁드려요 at the end. Common uses: 처음 뵙겠습니다. 잘 부탁드려요. (Nice to meet you. Please take good care of me.) or 앞으로 잘 부탁드려요. (Please take good care of me going forward.).

examples.en: Nice to meet you. Please take good care of me.
Please take good care of me going forward.
We'll be working together. Please take care of me.

description: Say what food you want to eat right now. Just place a noun before 먹고 싶어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 삼겹살 먹고 싶어요. (I want to eat samgyeopsal.) or 냉면 먹고 싶어요. (I want to eat naengmyeon.).
Say what you cannot eat due to allergy or preference. Say what you need, then add 못 먹어요 at the end. Common uses: 매운 거 못 먹어요. (I can't eat spicy food.) or 조개 못 먹어요. (I can't eat shellfish.).
Ask permission before eating something. Just place a noun before 먹어도 돼요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 이거 먹어도 돼요? (Is it okay to eat this?) or 여기서 먹어도 돼요? (Is it okay to eat here?).

examples.en: Is it okay to eat this?
Is it okay to eat here?
Is it okay to eat all of this?

description: Ask permission to call someone by a certain name. Just place a noun before 불러도 돼요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 언니라고 불러도 돼요? (Is it okay to call you 언니?) or 오빠라고 불러도 돼요? (Is it okay to call you 오빠?).

examples.en: Is it okay to call you 언니?
Is it okay to call you 오빠?
Is it okay to call you by your name?

description: Say you'd like to come back to a place again. Just place a noun before 또 오고 싶어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 여기 또 오고 싶어요. (I want to come here again.) or 한국에 또 오고 싶어요. (I want to come back to Korea.).

examples.en: I want to come here again.
I want to come back to Korea.
I want to come to this restaurant again.

description: Tell a driver where you want to be taken. Just place a noun before 까지 가 주세요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 공항까지 가 주세요. (Please take me to the airport.) or 명동까지 가 주세요. (Please take me to Myeongdong.).

examples.en: Please take me to the airport.
Please take me to the hotel.

description: Tell a friend casually that they just need to do one thing. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 이 버튼 누르면 돼. 쉬워. (Just press this button. It's easy.) or 여기서 왼쪽으로 꺾으면 돼. (Just turn left from here.).

examples.en: Just press this button. It's easy.
Just write your name and phone number.

description: Ask how long something takes. Use when waiting, traveling, or estimating time. Say 얼마나 걸려요? after describing the activity.

examples.en: How long does it take to get home?
How long do I have to wait?
